commit it, and report. Read this entire brief, then the repository AGENTS.md
and its relevant routed guidance. Do not stop at a survey or plan. If the issue
and repository genuinely leave a decision open, ask the judge one specific

# Working agreement

Your repository is the `bifrost` checkout under /workspace in your own container
(mj 2.10.0 places it at /workspace/<workspace id>/bifrost; `ls /workspace/*/bifrost`
finds it). The judge is Claude Fable.
All competing lanes receive this identical brief. Do not inspect other lanes,
their sessions, the judge's private files, or evaluation results about this issue.
Before investigation, verify your checkout has no tracked or untracked changes,
fetch origin, and check out this exact commit detached: 18fa60ee98f92a8dca58ffbd3a5d949adb30ee19
The detached checkout is explicitly authorized for this evaluation. Report its
full hash. Do not merge newer master or change the base during your initial run.

Work only in your container. Commit your changes on the detached HEAD, with
real messages. Do not push, create branches or PRs, edit issue labels, or post
GitHub comments. The judge exports your commits. Commit all intended work before
your final report; never stage unrelated files or use git add -A.
Do not write to any memory directory or MEMORY.md: that pool is shared across
sessions and harnesses. Keep discoveries in your report. Do not read other
evaluation sessions or their reports. Do not launch subagents; do the entire
solution in this lane, so every configuration has the same delegation policy.

Use plain cargo and the repository testing guidance. Clear JAVA_HOME and set
BIFROST_PARALLELISM=1 and RAYON_NUM_THREADS=1. Let nextest own concurrency;
pass --max-fail 100. Run relevant crate and integration suites. Changes under a
language's graph code or analysis usages require that language's usage and issue
suites plus cargo nextest run --max-fail 100 -p brokk-bifrost-analysis --lib.
Run cargo clippy --workspace --all-targets --all-features -- -D warnings and
format changed files. Do not reduce nextest concurrency without measured resource
exhaustion. Report pre-existing failures only after checking the same base.
The harness fails a turn after 10 minutes without activity, so never block on
one command for longer than 5 minutes: run long builds and suites in the
background or with a timeout of at most 300000 ms and poll their output.
No notification arrives between turns: never end your turn to wait for a
background command, because nothing will wake you. Poll it yourself in the
foreground, in waits of at most 5 minutes, and keep the turn running until the
FINAL REPORT is written.
Never run shared-cache GC or delete another session's build targets. If disk
pressure requires isolated storage, use the repository's managed target helper.

Fix causes with tree-sitter and analyzer structures, not source-text parsing or
regex fallbacks. Use assertions for construction invariants, iterative traversal
for deep trees, plain ASCII, and the existing shared helpers. Demonstrate a
production-shaped regression failing before and passing after the fix.
Read relevant architecture chapters before changing identities, cache, usage,
dataflow, semantic models or results. Bump the language extraction epoch when
the persisted language facts change; do not bump it for query-only changes.
Use an ExecPlan under .agents/plans only when the repository requires one.

External evidence repositories are not preinstalled: fetch the issue's pinned
commits under /workspace/evidence, outside this checkout. Use a fresh analyzer
cache at /workspace/cache when needed. Validate the actual witnesses and census
coverage, not merely a lower finding count caused by sampling or suppression.

Base commit (checked out detached, verified clean before work): `18fa60ee98f92a8dca58ffbd3a5d949adb30ee19`
Final commit on detached HEAD: `3517a70de3b893b312ac403baac018b63be65602` — "Close recursive SCC fixed points by discharging unlowered implicit aborts (#3528)"

## 1. Confirmed cause with structured evidence

The three v0.8.0 recursive templates were not blocked by the dataflow proof; they were blocked by an **open exceptional-exit boundary row** that only becomes load-bearing inside a recursive SCC.

- Base kernel reports (`/workspace/logs/before_reports`, `tool_build_identity = 18fa60ee…`) show the positives retaining the witness `Controlled input reaches the benchmark sink` while the run stays `inconclusive`, with exactly the diagnostics the issue quotes: `taint analysis is incomplete after reaching a fixed point: 3 unproven edge(s), 3 partial edge(s), and 2 open boundary row(s)` for `mutual-recursive-transform`, and `2 unproven edge(s), 2 partial edge(s), and 1 open boundary row(s)` for `recursive-carry` / `recursive-payload-transform`; the paired negatives carry the same incompleteness.
- Structured probe evidence (env-gated coverage probe, removed before commit; `/workspace/probe/logs/before-fx/*.stderr`): every unproven/partial row is an `ExceptionalReturn` edge whose origin is a `CallSiteId`, rejected with `callee-exit evidence does not prove this Exceptional completion returns to its caller: unsupported exceptional_control_flow: implicit exceptions from runtime coercion or operator dispatch are not yet lowered`; both open boundary rows are `Semantic(Unsupported { capability: ExceptionalControlFlow })` at each procedure's exceptional exit point (`ProgramPointId(2)`), where the plan records `abort_user_code=false`.
- Root cause: the C#, JavaScript, and Python adapters publish an `ExceptionalControlFlow` / `Unsupported` gap for a *represented* operator or comparison whose abort edge they do not lower (JS `+`, C# `+`/`checked`/`is`-pattern/subscript/cast, Python truth-test and comparison dispatch). That gap carried `SemanticGapDischarge::None`, so the exit-boundary classifiers (`semantic/icfg.rs::matched_return_gaps_are_implicit_abort_only`, `value_flow/plan.rs::exceptional_return_edge_is_abort_only` and `exceptional_exit_boundary_is_abort_only`) could not see that the omitted transfer only unwinds. Nonrecursive callees absorb this ubiquitous gap; a recursive call turns the callee's exceptional exit into a return edge inside the SCC, and the plan-wide `abort_paths_only_unwind()` requirement then never holds, so the fixed point is reached with the boundary still open. Rust already had the rule (`be1fb5f0b`), which is why Rust was not affected.
- Soundness: the discharge is granted only when the throw cannot enter handler or cleanup user code, so a retained witness cannot force `reached` while coverage is incomplete; that is pinned by the new `try/catch` and unresolved-target rows.

## 2. Changes and reasons

- `crates/bifrost-analysis/src/analyzer/semantic/cfg.rs` (+31): new `ProcedureCfgBuilder::throw_completion_leaves_procedure(scope)`, an iterative scope-chain walk — `Function` returns true, `Disconnected | Handler | Cleanup` return false, `Yieldable | Breakable | Loop` are transparent, chain end returns false.
- `crates/bifrost-analysis/src/analyzer/semantic/lowering.rs` (+38): new `ProcedureLoweringSession::add_unlowered_implicit_exception_gap(...)`, which publishes the same `ExceptionalControlFlow` / `Unsupported` gap but sets `NonRejoiningExceptionalExit` exactly when that walk answers true, because the exact lowering scope has no active handler or cleanup user code.
- Call sites now pass the lowering scope and route through it: 6 in `csharp/semantic.rs`, 6 in `js_ts/semantic/control.rs`, 2 in `python/semantic.rs`. `rust/semantic.rs`'s `add_non_rejoining_exceptional_exit_gap` delegates to the same helper (behaviour preserved, gains the handler check), so all five front ends share one contract instead of two similar ones.

## 6. Draft GitHub approach comment

The three recursive templates DataFlowBench v0.8.0 added stayed inconclusive in C#, JavaScript, Python, and TypeScript even though the positive witness was retained, and the blocker was an open exceptional-exit boundary row rather than the propagation proof. The adapters publish an `ExceptionalControlFlow` unsupported gap for a represented operator or comparison whose abort edge they do not lower (JavaScript `+`, C# `+`/`checked`/pattern/subscript/cast, Python truth tests and comparisons), and that gap carried no discharge, so the exit classifier could not tell that the omitted transfer only unwinds. Without recursion the same gap is absorbed; inside a recursive SCC it keeps the boundary open, so the fixed point is reached while the run cannot be decisive. The fix adds one shared lowering helper that marks that gap as a non-rejoining exceptional exit exactly when the exact lowering scope has no active handler or cleanup frame, decided by an iterative walk of the scope chain; a scope that can catch or clean up keeps the plain gap, so a retained witness can never force `reached` while coverage is incomplete. Rust's existing non-rejoining rule now delegates to the same helper, so all five front ends share one contract, and because the discharge is derived at lowering time and is not persisted, no language extraction epoch moved. On the v0.8.0 kernels all 12 positives now complete as `reached` and all 12 paired negatives as `not-reached`, with no other row changed and no negative false positives before or after; the four-language total goes from 77/140 to 89/140 positives reached. New `suite_bench_policy` rows pin the templates plus nonrecursive, depth-limited, call-context, unresolved-target, object-state, and `try/catch` near misses in every affected language, so the closure cannot pass by smearing summaries across call contexts.
